questions.prompt: What are the three Air Force Core Values?
choices: Integrity First, Service Before Self, Excellence In All We Do
questions.explanation: The Core Values are Integrity First, Service Before Self, and Excellence In All We Do. "Honor, Courage, Commitment" belongs to the Navy and Marine Corps.

questions.prompt: On what date did the Air Force become a separate military service?
questions.explanation: The Air Force was established on September 18, 1947, under the National Security Act of 1947, which President Truman signed on July 26, 1947.

questions.prompt: Which law created the Department of the Air Force?
questions.explanation: The National Security Act of 1947 created the Department of the Air Force and the independent US Air Force.

questions.prompt: Who was the first Chief of Staff of the Air Force?
questions.explanation: General Carl A. Spaatz was the first Chief of Staff of the Air Force, starting in 1947.

questions.prompt: Who was the first Secretary of the Air Force?
questions.explanation: W. Stuart Symington was the first Secretary of the Air Force. James Forrestal was the first Secretary of Defense.

questions.prompt: When and where did the Wright brothers make the first powered, controlled airplane flight?
questions.explanation: Orville and Wilbur Wright flew on December 17, 1903, at Kill Devil Hills near Kitty Hawk, North Carolina.

questions.prompt: What was the first military aviation organization in the United States, formed in 1907?
choices: The Aeronautical Division of the US Army Signal Corps
questions.explanation: The Aeronautical Division of the Army Signal Corps was formed on August 1, 1907. It led to the Air Service, the Air Corps (1926), and the Army Air Forces (1941).

questions.prompt: Which early air power advocate was court-martialed in 1925 for criticizing military leaders' neglect of aviation?
questions.explanation: Brigadier General William "Billy" Mitchell was court-martialed in 1925. His ideas on independent air power were later largely vindicated.

questions.prompt: Who led the April 1942 raid on Tokyo by B-25 bombers launched from the aircraft carrier USS Hornet?
questions.explanation: Lieutenant Colonel James "Jimmy" Doolittle led the Doolittle Raid on April 18, 1942, and received the Medal of Honor.

questions.prompt: The Tuskegee Airmen were best known as:
choices: The first Black military aviators in the US armed forces
The first Air Force jet aerobatic team
The crew of the first B-29
The first Air Force pararescue unit
questions.explanation: The Tuskegee Airmen, trained at Tuskegee, Alabama, were the first Black military aviators in the US armed forces. Their 332nd Fighter Group was known as the "Red Tails."

questions.prompt: Who commanded the Tuskegee Airmen's 332nd Fighter Group and later became the first Black general in the US Air Force?
questions.explanation: Benjamin O. Davis Jr. commanded the 332nd and became the Air Force's first Black general officer. Daniel "Chappie" James Jr. became the first Black four-star general.

questions.prompt: Who first flew faster than the speed of sound, in the Bell X-1 in 1947?
questions.explanation: Captain Charles "Chuck" Yeager broke the sound barrier on October 14, 1947, in the Bell X-1 he named "Glamorous Glennis."

questions.prompt: The Berlin Airlift (1948 to 1949) was a response to:
choices: The building of the Berlin Wall
A Soviet blockade of the land routes into West Berlin
questions.explanation: When the Soviet Union blocked the roads, rails, and canals into West Berlin, US and allied aircraft flew in food and fuel for over a year. The Berlin Wall came later, in 1961.

questions.prompt: Who became the first woman to reach four-star general in the US Air Force, in 2012?
questions.explanation: General Janet Wolfenbarger became the Air Force's first female four-star general in 2012. Jeanne Holm was the Air Force's first female general officer.

questions.prompt: When did the Space Force become a separate service within the Department of the Air Force?
questions.explanation: The US Space Force was established on December 20, 2019. It is a separate service within the Department of the Air Force, like the Marine Corps within the Department of the Navy.

questions.prompt: The Airman's Creed was introduced in 2007. Which line is part of it?
choices: "I will never leave an Airman behind"
questions.explanation: "I will never leave an Airman behind" is part of the Airman's Creed, along with "I will never falter, and I will not fail."

questions.prompt: What is the official Air Force motto, adopted in 2010?
questions.explanation: "Aim High... Fly-Fight-Win" became the official motto in 2010. The others were recruiting slogans.
